title: Titanium Spinal Interbody Cage
function: Lumbar interbody fusion cage with porous lattice
alloyReason: Ti-6Al-4V ELI (Extra Low Interstitials, ASTM F136 / ISO 5832-3) is the medical-grade standard for permanent implantable devices. Its lower oxygen (<0.13%) and iron (<0.25%) content provides superior fracture toughness and fatigue resistance compared to standard Grade 5, making it mandatory for orthopedic and spinal implants.
commonFailures: Surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (ASTM F86)
Thread damage from improper installation torque exceeding recommended values
Galvanic corrosion at interface with dissimilar metals in electrolyte environments

faq.q: What is a titanium spinal interbody cage?
faq.a: A titanium spinal interbody cage is a precision-machined spine fixation component used in lumbar interbody fusion cage with porous lattice. Manufactured from Ti-6Al-4V ELI (ASTM F136) for optimal strength, corrosion resistance, and weight savings.

faq.q: What standards apply to titanium spinal interbody cage?
faq.a: Titanium Spinal Interbody Cage is manufactured to ASTM F136 / ISO 5832-3 (Ti-6Al-4V ELI) or ASTM F1295 (Ti-6Al-7Nb) for medical implants. This requires oxygen <0.13%, iron <0.25%, and 100% traceability with MTC per batch.

faq.q: How is titanium spinal interbody cage manufactured?
faq.a: Titanium Spinal Interbody Cage is manufactured using CNC turning. Critical process controls include tool path optimization, coolant temperature management, and dimensional verification at each operation.

faq.q: What is the most common issue with titanium spinal interbody cage?
faq.a: The most common issue is surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (astm f86). Mitigation includes proper process control, material certification, and adherence to recommended installation procedures and torque values.
